content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (especially > -0.5) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent price spikes, then forecasts a sharp drop that doesn’t materialize.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction — model often misses the true turning point by 3–5 days.
- When sentiment turns negative after a spike, model delays correction; true price drops faster than forecasted.
- Model underestimates downward momentum in the final 5–7 days of the 30d horizon, especially when sentiment is negative.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — sentiment history suggests model is overly optimistic in first 5–7 days of forecast window.
